newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares end off for sixth straight session.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares end off for sixth straight session.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed lower for the sixth successive session Thursday in thin trading affected by falls on Wall Street, brokers said.
The market's 19-share index slipped 0.51 percent to 4,557.16, as 23 stocks fell, seven rose and 11 closed flat.
Brokers attributed some of the losses to foreigners selling stocks with American Depository Receipts (ADRs) during a bad day on Wall Street.
"There was pressure to sell stocks like Mantex and Sudamtex B. The selling was by foreigners because the ADRs were falling," said Boris Molina of the Merinvest brokerage.
Brokers added that foreign investors had been wary since the government's decision to postpone the privatization of Banco de Venezuela last Wednesday.
The postponement started the market's slide and "reminded foreigners that investment in countries like Venezuela is risky," Molina said.
Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas fell 5.45 bolivars to 385.55 bolivars and steel company Sivensa fell 3.65 bolivars to 286.10 bolivars.
Trading volume was well down from recent sessions at 1.646 billion bolivars ($3.5 million), the exchange said.
